name: Continental Simos PCR2.1 (VAG 1.6 / 2.0 TDI common rail)

read_methods.notes: Per OpenTune's siemens-pcr21 definition: calibration flashing over OBD, complete original via bench/boot read. Bench over CAN (ecupinouts).

notes: Continental unit for EA189 1.6 TDI (and some 2.0 TDI) common rail, alternative to the Bosch EDC17C46. Processor per a programming-module vendor's compatibility list (TC1796, 2 MB internal flash); OpenTune's ecudef flash_size is still a family placeholder. Pinout comes from a single source.

pins.note: Source labels it only '+12 V'; on the related VAG units T94-5 is terminal 15.

bench.notes: ecupinouts: tie +12 V to T94-5, T94-87 and T94-92, ground T94-1, CAN-H T94-68 / CAN-L T94-67.
bench.resistor_notes: Put a 120 ohm resistor across CAN-H/CAN-L if your interface does not terminate.

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.
